scope: Contended five-second Linux pilot with two complete development repetitions and a documented provenance amendment. Native results independently checked; external answers tool-reported. No idle-host, held-out or novelty claim.

provenance_amendment.reason: The frozen required_file_sha256 and inherited runtime inventory omitted the Z3 executable used by SMPT. Both block audits therefore fail its identity lookup; all other frozen checks pass.
provenance_amendment.acceptance_rule: Rerun the unchanged auditor and require exactly the original two missing-pin issues, identical recorded evidence hashes and block results. Verify launch execution -> capability -> capability environment hashes, matching qualification archive bytes, and identical Z3 observations in both terminal-bound block environments. Permit no other issue.
provenance_amendment.limitation: Z3 identity was recorded before competitive launch but omitted from enforced file pins. Matching observations do not prove pin enforcement or immutable executable identity between recorded checks. Do not describe this as an originally complete freeze.
provenance_amendment.preserved: Original failed audit, plan, source, admission rules, row data, terminal artifacts, arithmetic and frozen analysis sources remain unchanged. No measurement is replaced or rerun.
provenance_amendment.reporting_scope: Contended pilot. Saved load averages and cross-repeat wall-time variation prevent an idle-host timing claim.

host_contention.caveat: The recorded one-minute load averages were 34.37 and 25.06 on 32 logical CPUs. Each tool was 1.41–1.82 times slower in repeat 1 on its own common-solved queries. This is a contended pilot, not an idle-host measurement; CPU affinity and the workspace workload gate did not establish host-wide isolation. Timings and deadline-sensitive coverage should not be treated as an uncontended comparison. The provenance amendment does not repair the idle-host launch objective or certify idle-host protocol conformance.
